intro: En A2 empiezas a contar historias: lo que pasó, cómo era, qué vas a hacer y qué has hecho ya. Comparas cosas, hablas de cantidades y das consejos con los verbos modales.
goals: Contar lo que pasó con verbos irregulares, preguntas y negaciones en pasado.
Comparar personas y cosas con comparativos y superlativos.
Hablar del futuro con going to y will.
Usar some, any, much, many y a lot of con lo contable y lo incontable.
Decir qué has hecho ya con el presente perfecto y dar consejos con should, must y have to.

lessons.title: El pasado simple a fondo
lessons.summary: Irregulares frecuentes, preguntas con did y cómo contar una historia.

sections.heading: Los irregulares que más se usan
body: Los verbos irregulares no siguen la regla de -ed; su pasado hay que memorizarlo. Buena noticia: los más frecuentes son pocos y aparecen todo el tiempo.

sections.heading: Preguntas y negaciones
body: Did sirve para todas las personas, y el verbo vuelve a la forma base: Did she buy it? She didn't buy it. Las palabras interrogativas van delante: What did you do? Where did they go?
Was y were no necesitan did: Were you at home? I wasn't there.

examples.en: Were they happy? Yes, they were.

sections.tip: Did + forma base: Did you went? y Did you bought? son errores.

sections.heading: Contar una historia
body: Para ordenar lo que pasó se usan first (primero), then (luego), after that (después de eso), finally (al final). Las expresiones de tiempo van al principio o al final: Last summer we went to Peru. We went to Peru last summer.

examples.en: First we had breakfast, then we went to the museum.
examples.es: Primero desayunamos, luego fuimos al museo.

examples.en: After that, we took a taxi home.
examples.es: Después de eso, tomamos un taxi a casa.

exercises.prompt: She ___ a letter to her grandmother.
___ you see the match last night?

exercises.es: Nos fuimos temprano porque estábamos cansados.
answers: We left early because we were tired.

lessons.title: Comparativos y superlativos
lessons.summary: Más grande que, el más grande. Y los irregulares good, bad, far.

sections.heading: Comparar: más que
body: Con adjetivos cortos (una sílaba) se añade -er + than: taller than, older than. Si termina en -y, cambia a -ier: happier. Si termina en vocal + consonante, se dobla: bigger, hotter.
Con adjetivos largos (dos sílabas o más) se usa more + adjetivo + than: more expensive than, more interesting than.

examples.en: My brother is taller than me.
examples.es: Mi hermano es más alto que yo.

examples.en: This book is more interesting than that one.
examples.es: Este libro es más interesante que ese.
Hoy hace más calor que ayer.

sections.heading: El superlativo: el más
body: Con adjetivos cortos: the + adjetivo + -est (the tallest, the biggest). Con largos: the most + adjetivo (the most expensive). Suele ir con in (the best in the world) o of (the youngest of the family).

examples.en: She is the best student in the class.
examples.es: Ella es la mejor estudiante de la clase.

examples.en: It's the most beautiful city I know.
examples.es: Es la ciudad más bonita que conozco.
Esta es la opción más barata.

sections.tip: Good, bad y far son irregulares: better/best, worse/worst, farther/farthest. Nunca «more good».

sections.heading: Tan… como y menos… que
body: Para decir que dos cosas son iguales: as + adjetivo + as (as tall as). Para decir que no lo son: not as … as (not as expensive as). «Menos que» se dice less … than, y con adjetivos cortos se prefiere not as … as.

examples.en: He is as tall as his father.
examples.es: Él es tan alto como su padre.

examples.en: This hotel isn't as expensive as that one.
examples.es: Este hotel no es tan caro como ese.

examples.en: The second film was less interesting.
examples.es: La segunda película fue menos interesante.

exercises.prompt: A car is ___ (expensive) than a bike.
Today is the ___ (hot) day of the year.

exercises.es: Mi hermana es más joven que yo.
Esta película es tan buena como la primera.
answers: This film is as good as the first one.
This movie is as good as the first one.
This film is as good as the first.

lessons.title: El futuro: going to y will
lessons.summary: Planes, predicciones y decisiones del momento.

sections.heading: Going to: planes e intenciones
body: Be going to + verbo expresa planes decididos de antemano y predicciones con pruebas a la vista (nubes negras: it's going to rain). Se conjuga to be: I'm going to study, she's going to travel.

examples.en: I'm going to visit my grandparents on Sunday.
examples.es: Voy a visitar a mis abuelos el domingo.

examples.en: They're going to buy a house.
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
Are you going to come? No, I'm not.

sections.heading: Will: predicciones, promesas y decisiones
body: Will + verbo (sin to) sirve para predicciones sin pruebas (I think it will be sunny), promesas (I'll call you), ofrecimientos (I'll help you) y decisiones tomadas en el momento (I'll have the soup, please). Negación: won't.

examples.en: I'll help you with the bags.
Will you be at the party? Yes, I will.

sections.tip: Para quedar con alguien, el presente continuo también vale como futuro: I'm meeting Ana at six.

sections.heading: Expresiones de futuro
body: Tomorrow, next week, next year, in two days, this weekend, soon (pronto), later (más tarde). Van al principio o al final de la frase.

examples.en: Next year I'm going to learn to drive.
examples.es: El año que viene voy a aprender a conducir.

exercises.explanation: Plan decidido de antemano: going to.

exercises.prompt: The phone is ringing. I ___ answer it.

answers: I think it will be cold tomorrow.
I think it'll be cold tomorrow.
I think tomorrow will be cold.

lessons.title: Contable e incontable: some, any, much, many
lessons.summary: Agua, pan y dinero no se cuentan. ¿Cuánto hay?

sections.heading: Qué se cuenta y qué no
body: Los sustantivos contables tienen plural y van con a/an y números: an apple, three apples. Los incontables no tienen plural ni llevan a/an: water, bread, money, information, advice, furniture, news.
Para contar lo incontable se usa una medida: a glass of water, a piece of advice, a slice of bread.

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water?
She gave me a piece of advice.

sections.tip: Information, advice, furniture y news son incontables en inglés aunque en español los contemos: «una información» es a piece of information.

sections.heading: Some y any
body: Some en afirmativas (there's some milk, I have some friends) y en ofrecimientos o peticiones (Would you like some tea? Can I have some water?). Any en negativas y preguntas (I don't have any money, do you have any brothers?).

examples.en: There are some eggs in the fridge.

sections.heading: Much, many, a lot of y few, little
body: Many con contables y much con incontables, sobre todo en preguntas y negativas: How many people? How much time? Not much money. En afirmativas se prefiere a lot of (o lots of) con los dos: a lot of people, a lot of time.
A few (unos pocos) con contables y a little (un poco) con incontables: a few friends, a little sugar.

examples.en: How many brothers do you have?
I have a lot of work and a little free time.
examples.es: Tengo mucho trabajo y un poco de tiempo libre.

exercises.prompt: There aren't ___ chairs in the room.
How ___ students are there in your class?

answers: I need a piece of advice.
exercises.explanation: Advice es incontable: nada de «an advice».

lessons.title: El presente perfecto: ya, todavía, alguna vez
lessons.summary: Have you ever been to London? I've just finished.

sections.heading: Formar el presente perfecto
body: Have/has + participio pasado. En los regulares el participio es igual al pasado (-ed); en los irregulares hay que aprenderlo: be → been, go → gone/been, see → seen, do → done, eat → eaten, write → written, take → taken.
Habla de experiencias sin decir cuándo (I have visited Rome) y de acciones recientes con efecto en el presente (I've lost my keys: no las tengo ahora).

sections.heading: Ever, never, just, already, yet
body: Ever (alguna vez) en preguntas: Have you ever been to Japan? Never (nunca) en afirmativas con sentido negativo: I've never eaten sushi. Just (acabar de): I've just arrived. Already (ya) en afirmativas: She's already left. Yet (todavía, ya) al final de negativas y preguntas: I haven't finished yet. Have you eaten yet?

examples.en: Have you ever been to Japan?

sections.tip: Been o gone: She has gone to Paris (está allí ahora). She has been to Paris (fue y volvió).

sections.heading: Presente perfecto o pasado simple
body: Si dices cuándo (yesterday, last year, in 2015), usa el pasado simple: I saw her yesterday. Si no importa cuándo o la acción sigue conectada con ahora, el presente perfecto: I have seen her.

examples.en: Did you call him yesterday? Have you called him yet?

exercises.explanation: Just va entre have y el participio.
Ever va entre have y el participio.

lessons.title: Adverbios de frecuencia y de modo
lessons.summary: Siempre, a veces, nunca; rápidamente, bien, con cuidado.

sections.heading: Con qué frecuencia
body: Always (siempre), usually (normalmente), often (a menudo), sometimes (a veces), rarely (rara vez), never (nunca). Van antes del verbo principal y después de to be: I usually walk to work. She is always late.
Para preguntar: How often…? Respuestas: every day, once a week (una vez a la semana), twice a month (dos veces al mes), three times a year.

examples.en: I often go to the cinema.
How often do you exercise? Twice a week.
examples.es: ¿Con qué frecuencia haces ejercicio? Dos veces por semana.

sections.heading: Cómo se hace algo: adverbios de modo
body: Describen el verbo y suelen formarse con adjetivo + -ly: slow → slowly, quick → quickly, careful → carefully, easy → easily. Van después del verbo o del objeto: She speaks slowly. He drives the car carefully.
Irregulares: good → well, fast → fast, hard → hard, late → late. Hardly significa «apenas», no «duro».
sections.tip: Adjetivo para el sustantivo, adverbio para el verbo: a quick lunch, pero eat quickly.

sections.heading: Adverbios de intensidad
body: Very (muy), really (de verdad, muy), quite (bastante), too (demasiado), enough (suficiente, después del adjetivo): It's too hot. It isn't big enough.

examples.es: Esta habitación no es lo bastante grande.

exercises.explanation: Los adverbios de frecuencia van después de to be.

exercises.prompt: I go to the gym ___ a week. (dos veces)

lessons.title: Should, must y have to
lessons.summary: Deberías descansar. Tienes que ir. No debes fumar.

sections.heading: Should: consejos
body: Should + verbo base da consejos y opiniones: You should see a doctor. Negación: shouldn't. Pregunta: Should I call him?

sections.heading: Must y have to: obligación
body: Must expresa una obligación fuerte, a menudo del que habla o de una regla: You must wear a seatbelt. Have to expresa una obligación externa (trabajo, ley): I have to get up at six. En pasado solo existe had to.
Mustn't es prohibición (no debes); don't have to es que no hace falta (no tienes que).

examples.en: You must be quiet in the library.
examples.es: Debes guardar silencio en la biblioteca.

examples.en: I have to work on Saturday.
You don't have to come if you're tired.
examples.es: No tienes que venir si estás cansado.

sections.tip: Mustn't y don't have to no significan lo mismo: You mustn't pay (está prohibido) frente a You don't have to pay (es gratis).

sections.heading: Preguntas con have to
body: Have to funciona como un verbo normal: se pregunta y niega con do/does/did: Do you have to work? She doesn't have to study. Did they have to wait?

examples.en: Do I have to wear a tie?
We had to wait an hour.

exercises.prompt: You look tired. You ___ go to bed early.

exercises.explanation: No es necesario: don't have to.

exercises.prompt: Students ___ (must / not) use their phones in class. (prohibición)

lessons.title: El pasado continuo: estaba haciendo
lessons.summary: Qué estaba pasando cuando algo ocurrió.

sections.heading: Formar el pasado continuo
body: Was/were + verbo en -ing: I was sleeping, they were talking. Describe una acción en marcha en un momento del pasado. Negación: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Pregunta: Was she working?

examples.en: At eight o'clock I was having dinner.
They were waiting for the bus.
What were you doing at ten?

sections.heading: When y while
body: Lo típico es combinar los dos pasados: la acción larga en pasado continuo y la que la interrumpe en pasado simple. When va con el pasado simple; while con el continuo: I was cooking when the phone rang. While I was cooking, the phone rang.

examples.en: I was walking home when it started to rain.
examples.es: Iba caminando a casa cuando empezó a llover.

examples.en: While she was studying, her brother was playing video games.
examples.es: Mientras ella estudiaba, su hermano jugaba a los videojuegos.

examples.en: He fell while he was running.

sections.tip: Dos acciones largas a la vez: las dos en pasado continuo. Una interrumpe a otra: la corta en pasado simple.

sections.heading: Describir el escenario de una historia
body: El pasado continuo pinta el fondo: It was raining, people were running… y el pasado simple cuenta lo que pasó: Suddenly, I saw her.

examples.en: The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Then I heard a noise.
examples.es: El sol brillaba y los pájaros cantaban. Entonces oí un ruido.

exercises.explanation: Acción en marcha interrumpida: pasado continuo.

exercises.prompt: ___ she was cooking, the baby started to cry.
What were you ___ (do) when I called?

exercises.es: Estaba durmiendo cuando sonó el teléfono.

answers: While we were walking, it started to rain.
While we were walking it started to rain.
It started to rain while we were walking.

exam.prompt: She ___ me a present last week.
There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
You ___ wear a helmet. It's the law.
It's the ___ (good) book I've ever read.
She ___ (have to) get up early tomorrow.

exam.es: Voy a visitar a mis padres el domingo.

answers: I have never been to London.
You do not have to pay.
